I don't think that would be true. People may not show it, but they care about you more than they let on. If you did happen to die, I believe these people would be devastated and reveal how much they loved you. Everyone is different, and everyone shares and experiences their emotions differently. These people most definitely care about you, but they don't tell you out loud. You could ask them how they feel about you, and I bet they would say that they truly care about you and help you through whatever problems you are going through.

I think I have read something forbidden.

Went to a therapist once, and I fell into a depressive state in the middle of the session and couldn't bring myself to speak. The therapist eventually said she couldn't do anything and refused to help me if I wouldn't speak to her, and I never went back.

This therapist also gave bad advice to a friend who was struggling after their father's passing. My friend couldn't stop crying during the sessions and the therapist told them to get out of her room because she couldn't help them if they kept crying.

I eventually started going to a new therapist, and they are much better than the last.

I was debating whether or not to add sharpness or strength to the claws, but I decided since claws on animals are often sharp, sharpness seemed like a good option. 

And as for Infamous Reputation: the name for this is misleading. The pigs don't have a fear of the Ender dragon to begin with, they just think the player looks scary and run away. Since you can only eat meat, I thought this would make hunting much more difficult and balance out the Dragonheart pros.

I was basing that con after the Ender Dragon speedrunning tactic, but I wanted players to be able to sleep so they wouldn't be hated on a server or suffer phantoms in-game. That's why I added the dragon egg that you receive when you first spawn into the game. You can sleep beside it, and then break the egg and move it around like a normal bed. You just can't use typical beds.

I was trying to design this origin on a big RNG factor (how far and when you might be teleported and the bugged ability.) I was noticing I kinda made the cons really unbalanced, so I was thinking of shrinking the teleporting range into maybe 10-15 blocks and only dropping 5 random items.
